`BaseHandler.load_middleware` starts at the centre, the innermost layer, and works outwards (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).
Raising `MiddlewareNotUsed` lets a middleware take itself out according to configuration, and none of the middleware Django ships does so (`django/core/exceptions.py:MiddlewareNotUsed`).

It runs through the setting backwards, and it puts each `process_view` at the front of its list and each of the other two at the end of theirs (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

Every `process_exception` hook is filed synchronous, the handling of exceptions being still synchronous throughout (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`), and filing a coroutine function synchronous, `BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode` wraps it in `async_to_sync` ([Sync and async in one chain](async.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode`).

Every `process_exception` hook is filed synchronous, the handling of exceptions being still synchronous throughout (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`), and filing a coroutine function synchronous, `BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode` wraps it in `async_to_sync` ([Sync and async in one chain](async.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode`).

Under ASGI the centre calls the hooks from a thread, through `sync_to_async`, and an async hook is sent back to the event loop to run while that thread waits, a trip a synchronous hook does not make (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response_async`).
Under WSGI, unless a layer runs asynchronously, each call of the hook starts an event loop in a new thread (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:AsyncToSync.__call__`).

When the layer runs synchronously, `MiddlewareMixin.__call__` gives the request to `process_request`, if the class has one, and calls the layer inside only if that returned no response, which is how such a response skips the view; then it gives the response it holds, whichever made it, to `process_response`, if the class has one, and returns what that returns (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).

Django 1.10 shipped the new style, in a new setting, `MIDDLEWARE`, "to solve the lack of strict request/response layering" of the old (`docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

To carry the old hooks over, DEP 5 offered a mixin, `MiddlewareMixin`, "to ease providing the existing built-in middleware in both new-style and old-style forms, and to ease similar conversions of third-party middleware" (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`).
